parts.text:
6
A ball is thrown horizontally off a tall building. The ground is horizontal. Air resistance is
negligible.
Which statement about the motion of the ball is correct?
A
The acceleration of the ball is always at right angles to the path of the ball.
B
The ball follows a circular path until it hits the ground.
C
The ball has constant acceleration.
D
The ball’s time in the air is proportional to the velocity at which the ball is thrown.

hints: Notice the ball is thrown horizontally and air resistance is negligible, so identify the only force acting after release and its direction.
Connect that force to acceleration using $F = ma$: a constant vertical weight gives a constant vertical acceleration of about $9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Separate the motion into horizontal motion with no acceleration and vertical fall from rest, then ask which of the path shape, acceleration angle and flight time claims fits that model.
walkthrough: List the conditions: horizontal initial velocity, horizontal ground, and negligible air resistance, so the only force on the ball in flight is its weight vertically down.
Use Newton's second law $a = F/m$. Since weight $W = mg$ is constant in magnitude and direction, acceleration is constant $g$ vertically downward.

Resolve the motion: horizontally velocity stays constant because $a_x = 0$, while vertically the ball accelerates from zero initial vertical velocity, giving a parabolic path that gets steeper with time.
Check the other statements: the acceleration is not always perpendicular to the curved path, the path is not circular, and the fall time depends on building height, not on horizontal throw speed.
Only the constant-acceleration statement matches free-fall projectile motion. This is option C.

A.explanation: Acceleration is always vertically down at $g$, while the velocity direction curves downward, so it is at right angles to the path only at the instant of horizontal projection.

B.explanation: With constant horizontal velocity and uniformly accelerated vertical fall, the trajectory is parabolic, not part of a circle.

C.explanation: With air resistance negligible the only force is weight, so acceleration is constant $g$ vertically downward throughout the flight.

D.explanation: Time in the air is set by the vertical height fallen from rest, so it is independent of the horizontal throwing velocity.
